title: Zariski-to-etale comparison for the naive cotangent complex of schemes
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be the same morphism regarded as a morphism of representable algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On the Zariski site of $X_0$, put $A=f_0^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y_0}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X_0}$, using inverse image of ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] and the structure map $A\to B$. Let $\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X_0/Y_0}$ be the standard sheaf naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=K_B$ of [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison]: explicitly take the sheaf polynomial algebra $A[B]\twoheadrightarrow B$, its kernel $J$, and $[J/J^2\to\Omega_{A[B]/A}\otimes_{A[B]}B]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with $[h]\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1$. Let $\epsilon_X:X_{0,\mathrm{et}}\to X_{0,\mathrm{Zar}}$ be the canonical ringed-site morphism and $\epsilon_X^*M=\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon_X^{-1}\mathcal O_{X_0}}\epsilon_X^{-1}M$ its tensor pullback [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\epsilon_X^*\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X_0/Y_0}\simeq\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})$$
[def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here the left side is obtained by termwise tensor pullback. No finite-type, Noetherian, flatness or separatedness assumption on $f_0$ is imposed.

proof.text: The canonical comparison square for $f_0$ supplies compatible ring maps $\epsilon_X^{-1}A\to f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$ and $\epsilon_X^{-1}B\to\mathcal O_X$. Apply inverse-image invariance and the functorial polynomial-presentation map to obtain a chain map $c:\epsilon_X^*\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{X_0/Y_0}\to\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$. On presentations it sends $[b]$ to the variable indexed by its structural image; in degrees $-1,0$ it sends a relation to its image and $\mathrm dh\otimes a$ to $\mathrm d(h')\otimes a$. Thus the differential commutes with $c$, and every comparison is the specified canonical one. Exactness of $\epsilon_X^*$ ensures that its termwise interpretation is compatible with quasi-isomorphisms.

Fix $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_0$, put $\bar y=f_0\bar x$, and let $x,y$ be the underlying points. Set $R=\mathcal O_{Y_0,y}$, $T=\mathcal O_{X_0,x}$, $R'=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $T'=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$. The identity scheme charts identify $R',T'$ with the strict henselizations of $R,T$ selected by the residue embeddings in $\Omega$. The strict-local functoriality statement identifies $R'\to T'$ with the induced map of these strict henselizations: its maps to each pointed neighbourhood and its residue embedding are the prescribed ones. Since $f_0$ is a scheme morphism, $R\to T$ is local; there is no finite-type condition here.

Apply the pullback-stalk formula to $\epsilon_X$ at the point $p$ given by $\bar x$. The geometric stalk at $\bar x$ is inverse image along $\bar x_{\mathrm{et}}:\operatorname{Sh}(P_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, followed by $\Gamma(P,-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]; every etale $P$-scheme is a disjoint union of copies of $P$, so $\Gamma(P,-)$ identifies $\operatorname{Sh}(P_{\mathrm{et}})$ with $\mathbf{Set}$, compatibly with rings and modules. The image point $q=\epsilon_X\circ p$ is the Zariski point $x$: $\epsilon_X^{-1}H$ is the sheafification of $U\mapsto\varinjlim_{W\supseteq\operatorname{im}U}H(W)$, sheafification does not change geometric stalks [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk], and in the resulting double colimit the opens $W\ni x$, pointed by $\bar x$, are cofinal: a lift of $\bar x$ to $W$ exists exactly when $x\in W$, and each $(U,\bar u)$ maps to $(W,\bar x)$ when $W\supseteq\operatorname{im}U$. So $H_q=H_x$, and $(\epsilon_X^*\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}})_{\bar x}$ is $(\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}})_x\otimes_T T'$. Inverse-image invariance for the point $\{x\}\hookrightarrow X_0$ and the ordinary inverse-image stalk comparison ($A_x=R$) identify $(\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}})_x=\mathrm{NL}_{T/R}$. The same invariance for $\bar x_{\mathrm{et}}$ gives $(\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y})_{\bar x}=\mathrm{NL}_{T'/(f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_{\bar x}}$, and the etale inverse-image stalk comparison $(f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}=R'$ is multiplicative, being given on germs [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. All are identifications of the standard complexes, before passing to the derived category.

Under step 3, $c_{\bar x}$ is exactly $\mathrm{NL}_{T/R}\otimes_T T'\to\mathrm{NL}_{T'/R'}$. Indeed its polynomial generators are sent by $R\to R'$ and $[t]\mapsto[t']$; its relation and differential components are $[h]\otimes a\mapsto a[h']$ and $\mathrm dh\otimes a\mapsto\mathrm d(h')\otimes a$, the same formulas used in step 1. The strict-henselization comparison therefore makes this stalk map a quasi-isomorphism, using the compatible residue choices of step 2.

Geometric stalks of abelian etale sheaves are exact and jointly detect isomorphisms. Forgetting a module structure computes kernels and cokernels on the underlying abelian sheaves, so stalks commute with the cohomology of each complex. Step 4 says that every cohomology map of $c$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk; joint detection makes each cohomology map an isomorphism of sheaves (the inverse is automatically linear). Thus $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and becomes the asserted isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})$. The empty scheme has no stalks and all its module sheaves are zero, giving the same conclusion.
